Without an independent agent, \"seeing sees\" is incoherent — the act cannot perform itself.","madhyamaka":"Garfield: the verse targets the reification of the seer (draṣṭṛ). If the seer is just the act of seeing itself, there's no separate agent. If the seer is separate from seeing, it's a \"nonseeing seer\" — which is a contradiction. Either way, no independent seer can be established. Kalupahana connects this to the Ch. 2 mover argument: just as no mover exists apart from motion, no seer exists apart from seeing. Candrakīrti: the seer is an upādāya prajñapti (dependent designation), not an inherently existing agent.","quantum":"Quantum Contextuality / Kochen-Specker Theorem: Properties do not pre-exist measurement context. The quantum \"observer\" has no pre-existing state independent of the measurement context; the Buddhist \"seer\" has no pre-existing identity independent of the act of seeing. Both are contextually constituted, not independently real.","accessible":"Are you a \"listener\" when you're not listening to anything? The label \"listener\" only applies when you're actually listening. There's no hidden \"listener-essence\" inside you waiting to be activated. Similarly, \"seer\" is a label that applies only when seeing happens — no independent seer-entity exists.","twoTruths":"Conventionally, we say \"I see the tree\" — the seer functions perfectly. Ultimately, no seer-entity can be found apart from the act of seeing — the designation is purely contextual.","commonMisconception":"NOT denying that subjects perceive objects.
